labels.label: defi:causal_Ealpha

hypotheses.paper: the model space E^{1,2} (and its cones E_alpha)
hypotheses.note: R x X for any geodesic metric space X; Minkowski R^{1,n} for every n. Cones E_alpha (alpha != 2pi) and E_0 not covered: the next package instantiates Static.lean

read as the graph of a c-Lipschitz map for one c < 1 over a non-trivial segment (uniformly timelike). Not a restriction: it gives the same <<_U as 'speed < 1 at every point' in every open U (see findings and Static.lean SCOPE)

findings: Formalized for Minkowski space R^{1,n} (and every static R x X over a geodesic space): the relations defined by curves in every open set form a causality (axioms (a)-(c), << transitive, I^pm_U(x) open), as l.1336-1339 assert; the openness of I^pm needs the geodesic hypothesis (a perturbed endpoint is reached by a geodesic segment inside a ball of U). The sentence 'On any E>=0-manifold there is then a unique causal structure...' (l.1339-1341) is not addressed.

l.1337 does not define 'future chronological curve'. The uniform reading (c-Lipschitz for one c < 1) and the pointwise one (speed < 1 at every point, supremum possibly 1) define the same <<_U in every open U, so no question to the author is needed: a pointwise-timelike curve has strict chords d(gamma s, gamma s') < |s - s'|; a fine enough inscribed polygon of geodesic segments stays in a thickening of the compact graph, hence in U, and its finitely many slopes have a maximum c < 1. The argument is in prose (Static.lean SCOPE), not formalized; causallyArcConnected independently proves that staticLt U is equivalent to a chronal curve of Causal/Curves.lean in U. (Question withdrawn after audit.)

labels.label: rem:pushup

hypotheses.note: proved for every static spacetime, Minkowski included; E_alpha (alpha != 2pi) and E_0 not covered

findings: l.1375-1376 'the concatenation of a future causal curve with a future chronological one is future chronological' is false for the concatenated curve itself: a chronological curve followed by a null segment is not chronological (it has a null piece). What holds, and what the 'Equivalently' formula and defi:pushup need, is that the END POINTS are chronologically related in the same open set, through another curve: Lean re-times the concatenation (the chronological part sped up, the causal part slowed down) inside a tube of U (staticLt_of_staticLt_of_staticLe). Suggested wording: '...the end points of the concatenation of a future causal curve with a future chronological one are joined by a future chronological curve in the same open set.'

labels.label: cor:model_minimal

labels.label: lem:IJ_calc

hypotheses.note: Minkowski space and static spacetimes only; Z^+ = Z^- = M there, so the identity reads Int J^pm(p) = I^pm(p)

findings: Missing citation, not an error. The proof (l.1446-1447, l.1452-1454) passes from 'I^-(q) is non-empty' to 'q in Z^-' (and from non-empty chronological futures to Z^+ = E_kappa). That step is rem:absolutely_minimal_topological_spacetime (l.780-782), which applies because the models are absolutely minimal by cor:model_minimal (l.1386); Lean's proof goes the same way (AbsolutelyMinimal.mem_Zminus_iff). Suggested wording: '... so I^-(q) is non-empty and therefore, by Remark rem:absolutely_minimal_topological_spacetime and Corollary cor:model_minimal, q in Z^-(E_kappa).' For the static models Z^pm = M is also proved directly (mem_Zplus, mem_Zminus).

labels.label: prop:mesure_dieckmann_Lorentz

hypotheses.note: Minkowski space R^{1,n} only (the library has no Lorentzian manifolds): the row is 'stated on the Minkowski instance', not a statement for strongly causal Lorentzian manifolds

sorries.obstruction: a finite regular measure on R^{1+n}, positive on non-empty open sets, null on the frontier of I^pm(A) for EVERY A: the frontier of I^-(A) lies in the graph of the 1-Lipschitz x -> sup_{a in A} (a.1 - |x - a.2|), Lebesgue-null by Fubini; neither step is in mathlib at this pin. Everything else is proved: the proposition is reduced to this measure (minkowski_mesure_dieckmann_of)

findings: l.1058-1059 'one then checks easily that conditions 3. and 4. hold': condition 4 for an ARBITRARY A rests on the classical theorem that achronal boundaries are Lipschitz hypersurfaces (Hawking-Ellis, Prop. 6.3.1), hence Lebesgue-null; the paper's sentence stands once that fact is cited. Concretely, with K^pm(A) = I^pm(A) (push-up and Z^pm = M) condition 4 asks that mu not charge J^pm(A) \ I^pm(A), a subset of the frontier of the open past/future set I^pm(A). Condition 3 is elementary (J^-(q) \ J^-(p) contains a non-empty open set, exists_isOpen_subset_Jminus_diff). The sorry'd existence statement is true for every n, n = 0 included (a Gaussian), so it is not vacuous.
Row status for the ledger: stated, on the Minkowski instance only (hypothesis strengthened).

labels.label: theo:geroch
findings: Witness only (the theorem is WP-7's). DEC-15's counterexample is now a Lean theorem, with a LOCAL (absolutely minimal) causality, not Causality.ofRelation: on R^{1,n}, n >= 1 (n = 1: minkowski2_dec15), T(t,x) = t - g(x) with g(x) = max(0, min(<x,e>, 1)) (bounded, 1-Lipschitz, g(tau e) = tau on [0,1]) is a Cauchy time function in the DEC-10 sense, is not strictly increasing along <= ((0,0) <= (1,e), same T), and T^{-1}(0) contains the null segment {(tau, tau e)} and is not a Cauchy surface (DEC-14): the null line tau -> (tau, tau e), inextensible, meets it at least twice. This confirms why l.1300 'it suffices to take S = T^{-1}(0)' needs DEC-15. The time coordinate is a strictly increasing Cauchy time function (minkowski_time_strict), so (ii) as ruled is satisfiable there.

Lean declarations of this witness (not row decls, so as not to overwrite WP-7's theo:geroch row): Causal.minkowski_dec15, Causal.minkowski2_dec15, Causal.staticCausality.not_strict_and_not_isCauchySurface, Causal.staticCausality.isCauchyTimeFunction_sub, Causal.staticCausality.isTimeFunction_sub, Causal.staticCausality.tendsto_time_atTop, Causal.staticCausality.tendsto_time_atBot, Causal.staticCausality.inextensible_nullLine, Causal.minkowski_inextensible_nullLine, Causal.minkowski_time_strict, Causal.Causality.Inextensible.not_tendsto_atBot, Causal.Causality.Inextensible.not_tendsto_atTop, Causal.Causality.inextensible_of_unbounded.

labels.label: def:maximal_chain
findings: Witness only (the definition is Causal/Chains.lean's, OQ-17). As written, Minkowski space R^{1,n}, n >= 1 (indeed every static R x X with X geodesic with two points), has NO maximal causal chain: every open set contains two small balls at one time, spatially apart, with no causal relation between them (hasUnrelatedOpensIn), and not_isMaximalChain_of_hasUnrelatedOpensIn applies. Hence def:causally_connected fails in Minkowski space and def:causally_complete holds vacuously there (minkowski_not_causallyConnected, minkowski_causallyComplete). This is with the local causality of curves, so it is not an artefact of non-local causalities (kb/0019).

Lean declarations of this witness (not row decls, so as not to overwrite Causal/Chains.lean's def:maximal_chain row): Causal.minkowski_not_isMaximalChain, Causal.minkowski_not_causallyConnected, Causal.minkowski_causallyComplete, Causal.staticCausality.not_isMaximalChain, Causal.staticCausality.hasUnrelatedOpensIn.

hypotheses.note: Minkowski space of every dimension, and every static spacetime; the cones E_alpha, E_0 and the singular flat spacetimes are not covered. The Galileo half is Causal/Galileo.lean's

findings: The sentence 'the flat model spacetimes ... are strongly causal' (l.672-674) holds for Minkowski space: the vertical diamonds J((t-e,x),(t+e,x)) are causally convex and lie in the closed e-ball (stronglyCausal).

kb_proposals: The model spaces' causality lives in CausalScaffold.Static: staticCausality X over any GeodesicSpace X (relations by Lipschitz graphs in each open set); Minkowski = staticCausality (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)). The cone E_alpha should prove its local facts by charts to it or reuse StaticCurve/LipOn.
Past from future without a dual causality: a time flip (t,x) ↦ (−t,x) as a preimage of open sets (flipT, staticLt_flip_iff) gives isOpen_lt_left and the second push-up from the first.

Push-up by re-timing: speed the chronological part up, slow the causal part down, and keep the graph inside a thickening of the compact graph (IsCompact.exists_thickening_subset_open + mem_thickening_iff).

An inextensible curve over ℝ has no limit at either end under the hypotheses of extensible_of_tendsto (Causality.Inextensible.not_tendsto_atBot/atTop, by c ∘ log over ]0,∞[); a curve along which a ≤-monotone function is unbounded both ways is inextensible (inextensible_of_unbounded).
EuclideanSpace's MeasurableSpace instance needs import Mathlib.Analysis.Normed.Lp.MeasurableSpace; a causality on EuclideanSpace must be a noncomputable abbrev.
